key_insight: Task-specific quantum sensing algorithms achieve an optimal √N speedup over conventional frequency scanning for detection, search, and learning across N known candidate frequencies.
engineering_relevance: The approach could accelerate molecular screening with nitrogen-vacancy sensors and enable wireless communication in weak-signal regimes.
method: Model time-varying signals supported on a known set of N candidate frequencies.
Tailor optimal algorithms to Detection, Search, and Learning tasks.
Use a single qubit with π-pulse control for Detection and Search; use coherent quantum-computer processing for optimal Learning.
evidence_signal: End-to-end numerical simulations incorporating experimental imperfections predict up to two orders of magnitude speedup in Detection, alongside feasibility analyses for nitrogen-vacancy molecular screening.
watch_item: The reported Detection gains are simulation-based, and optimal Learning requires coherent quantum-computer processing beyond a single-qubit sensor.
paper_title: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
